# A negation's change, and cases into a stable conclusion

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`negation-change-and-stable-cases` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](negation-change-and-stable-cases.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> What ceases to be is the coming to be of its negation, and back where the determination is stable; a conclusion following from a proposition and from its failure holds wherever it is stable, the proposition undecided.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. What ceases to be is the coming to be of its negation, and what comes to be the ceasing of its negation, with no premise; read back, the determination must be stable where it is read; on a web, a formation ceasing is its inactivity coming to be. (`Becoming.CeasesToBe.not_comes`, `Becoming.ComesToBe.not_ceases`, `Becoming.ComesToBe.of_not`, `Becoming.CeasesToBe.of_not`, `Becoming.Web.ceasing_readings`)
2. A conclusion following from a proposition and from its failure holds wherever it is stable, the proposition left undecided; every negation and every equation of numbers is stable. (`Becoming.Decided.cases_stable`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; a determination is any predicate of steps; stability (double negation elimination at the point read) where stated.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That a determination is decided: only stability where read is used.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
